newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chubais hits Duma, says govt to rule alone.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chubais hits Duma, says govt to rule alone.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, irritated at the lower house of parliament's latest failure to approve economic reforms, said on Tuesday the government would have to push them through alone.

Asked whether ministers were pushing for President Boris Yeltsin to dissolve the communist-dominated State Duma, Chubais told reporters the chamber had shown itself incapable of working but such a decision was the president's only.

Chubais, whom Yeltsin charged with leading a new round of free market reforms in March, said the government had done all it could to compromise with the Duma but parliament had shown itself unable to take difficult decisions and had preferred to rise for its two-month summer recess on Tuesday.

"If the Duma does not take on responsibilities, it makes one doubt whether it is capable of working," he said. "Out of three questions, the Duma completely failed to take a decision on two of them...It suggests the majority in the Duma is not capable of taking political responsibility to the extent demanded today."

The Duma approved the government's new tax code last week but on Monday voted down a bill to slash 1997 spending and on Tuesday rejected the bulk of the government's package of welfare reforms and spending cuts.

Chubais, who has previously hinted that Yeltsin might consider dissolving the Duma, said government experts were already working on plans that would allow the administration to fulfil promises to pay off arrears on pensions and other benefits and restore order to the state finances.
